draft.title: Factors that shift demand
card: A change in a good's own price moves buyers along the demand curve. A change in any other factor shifts the whole curve. A shift right means more is demanded at every price. A shift left means less.
Higher disposable income (income after tax) usually raises demand for most goods. A rise in popularity, or tastes moving towards a good, shifts its demand right.

Substitutes can replace each other, such as tea and coffee. If the price of one rises, demand for the other rises. Complements are used together, such as printers and ink. If the price of one rises, demand for the other falls.
Lower interest rates make borrowing cheaper, which can raise demand for goods bought on credit. A larger population and higher consumer confidence (optimism about the economy) can also raise demand.
draft.remember: Only a change in the good's own price moves along the curve. Other factors shift the whole curve.

a.q: The price of coffee rises sharply, and cafés in Geelong find that more customers buy tea at every price. What happened to the demand for tea?
opts: It shifted right, because a substitute became dearer
It shifted left, because a substitute became dearer
It shifted right, because a complement became dearer
It moved along the curve, because the price of tea rose
a.why: Coffee and tea are substitutes, so a dearer coffee sends buyers to tea at every price. That shifts the whole demand curve for tea right. The price of tea did not change, so there is no movement along the curve.
a.clue: Tea and coffee can replace each other, and tea's own price did not change.

b.q: Printer prices in Melbourne rise, and fewer people buy printers. What is the likely effect on demand for printer ink, and why?
opts: It shifts left, because ink is a complement to printers
It shifts right, because ink is a substitute for printers
It shifts left, because the price of ink has risen
It shifts right, because ink is a complement to printers
b.why: Ink is used together with printers, so it is a complement. Fewer printers bought means less ink wanted at every price, so ink demand shifts left. Ink's own price did not change, so the cause is not a movement along the curve.
b.clue: Ink is used together with printers, and ink's own price has not changed.

a.best: It shifted right, because a substitute became dearer

b.best: It shifts left, because ink is a complement to printers
